jobs.description: Employer: Fastflo Expires: 10/05/2026 Sales Intern (BRD)Fastflo | Remote | Part-time or Full-time | Base + CommissionAbout FastfloFastflo is a VC-backed B2B SaaS startup built at the Harvard Innovation Labs. We're changing how companies hire frontline workers: instead of forcing candidates through clunky web forms, applications happen natively inside iMessage and other messaging apps. The result is that around 80% of candidates finish their application, versus roughly 15% on traditional flows. We recently closed our seed round and count global enterprise brands and multi-location franchise operators among our customers.We're now scaling our sales pipeline, and that's where you come in.The RoleYou will own the very top of our sales engine. We hand you qualified lead lists; your job is to get decision makers on the phone and book meetings for our closing team. You are not selling on these calls, and you're not expected to. Your single goal is simple and measurable: turn a qualified lead into a booked meeting. Our team takes it from there and closes the deal.This is the fastest possible education in startup sales. You'll learn how to open a cold call, handle a brush-off, earn thirty seconds of attention from a busy operator, and convert it into a calendar invite. These are skills that compound for the rest of your career, and you'll build them with direct coaching from our founder and sales leadership, not from the back row of a large sales floor.Booking meetings is where you start, not where you stop. Prove yourself on the phones and your scope grows with you: sitting in on the sales calls you booked, running parts of discovery and demos, and taking on responsibilities across the sales cycle and the wider business. At a startup this size, the people who deliver get handed more, quickly.What You'll DoCold call decision makers from qualified lead lists we provideBook discovery meetings for the closing team and hand off clean contextTrack your outreach and results in our CRMRefine call scripts and openers with the team based on what's actually workingGet direct visibility into how booked meetings turn into closed dealsWhat Success Looks LikeQualified meetings booked. That's the metric. You'll have a clear weekly target, full transparency on your numbers, and commission tied directly to the meetings you put on the calendar.Who Thrives HereCurrently pursuing or recently completed a bachelor's or master's degreeComfortable picking up the phone and talking to strangers, or genuinely eager to become comfortable fastResilient: you can hear "no" ten times and dial the eleventh number with energyCoachable, organized, and self-directed in a remote environmentNo prior sales experience required. We provide training, scripts, and ongoing coaching.Compensation & LogisticsBase pay (hourly) plus commissionAcademic credit available where your program allows, in addition to compensationFully remotePart-time or full-time depending on your availabilityStrong performers have a clear path to a Summer 2026 internship or a full-time role

jobs.description: Employer: Wellington Management Company LLP Expires: 10/06/2026 WELLINGTON MANAGEMENTWellington Management offers comprehensive investment management capabilities that span nearly all segments of the global capital markets. Our investment solutions, tailored to the unique return and risk objectives of institutional clients in more than 50 countries, draw on a robust body of proprietary research and a collaborative culture that encourages independent thought and healthy debate. This 10-week paid internship provides hands-on experience, mentorship, and exposure to the investment management industry. You will have the opportunity to indicate your preferences during the application process. Client Platform – The Client Platform is a global team focused on building and deepening relationships with prospects, clients, and consultants. Working closely with Wellington's investment professionals, the team helps clients navigate complex investment challenges, understand their unique objectives, and identify the investment strategies, portfolios, and solutions best suited to their needs. The platform includes professionals across business development, relationship management, and product management who support a diverse range of institutional investors, including public pension funds, central banks, insurance companies, endowments, foundations, retirement plan sponsors, and mutual fund sponsors. Responsibilities may include analyzing new business opportunities by region or channel, supporting business analytics, conducting competitive analysis and due diligence, engaging with Wellington’s evolving technologies and client-related applications, and helping evaluate investment opportunities. Finance – The Finance team provides financial stewardship and strategic support across Wellington's global business. Through financial planning and analysis, budgeting, forecasting, expense management, tax, and corporate finance activities, the team helps guide business decisions, allocate resources, and support the firm's long-term growth. Interns may contribute to financial analysis and modeling, budgeting processes, management reporting, tax research, and other projects that provide insight into how a global investment management firm operates. Global Operations – This function drives the firm's operational edge to exceed the investment and service expectations of our clients worldwide. Working across investment, client, and infrastructure teams, the group designs and executes the processes, controls, and infrastructure that support Wellington's world-class investment strategies and client relationships. The team plays a critical role in supporting client onboarding and servicing, investment activities, operational reporting, and responding to the evolving needs of our global client base. Interns will gain a practical understanding of how operational processes are built to deliver scalability, risk mitigation, service excellence, and a high-quality client experience. Legal, Compliance & Risk – Help the firm operate effectively in a complex regulatory environment with evolving compliance programs, you will contribute to the completion of risk-mitigating projects, and conduct analysis and reporting. Responsibilities may include tagging and analyzing key risk management metrics, gaining proficiencies in regulatory requirements of regimes applicable to a US investment adviser, assisting with due diligence process for new and critical vendors, and assisting with the testing of control design and effectiveness. Investment Implementation & Trading – Opportunity to gain practical experience in the dynamic world of markets and trading. Responsibilities may include supporting the firm’s domestic and international post-execution trade activities, interacting with traders and brokers, and conducting trading data analysis. You will gain a solid foundation in trading and trade confirmation practices associated with today’s global financial markets. You will learn about a variety of markets, the role of trading at Wellington, the trade lifecycle, and how we work with portfolio managers who invest on behalf of our clients. Additionally, you will gain experience in industry applications such as Bloomberg, and CTM. We look for:Current sophomore and junior undergraduate students from all academic majors working toward a bachelors degreeStrong communication, attention to detail, organization, and problem-solving skillsCurious and adaptable, with an interest in leveraging emerging technologies and AI tools to improve efficiency, enhance decision-making and discover smarter ways of workingInterest in business, finance, or operationsParticipation in on-campus activities, leadership roles, volunteer opportunities and work experiences Ability to work collaboratively in a team environmentNo prior finance experience is required. This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Application Deadline: October 2, 2026 JOB TITLEBusiness Undergraduate Summer Internship LOCATION280 Congress Not sure you meet 100% of our qualifications? That’s ok. If you believe that you could excel in this role, we encourage you to apply and welcome a chance to review your background. We are dedicated to building and maintaining a diversified workforce and considering a broad array of candidates with a variety of skill, workplace experiences, and backgrounds. As an equal opportunity employer, Wellington Management considers all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, religion, creed, national origin, age, ancestry, disability (physical or mental), medical condition, citizenship, marital status, pregnancy, veteran or military status, genetic information or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. We strive to pay employees fairly and competitively across all levels and roles. The base salary range for this position is: no range availableThis range takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered when making compensation decisions, including but not limited to skill sets; role; skills and experience; certifications; and education. This range is an estimate, and further details on salary and total compensation aspects will be shared with candidates during the recruitment process. Base salary is only one component of Wellington’s total compensation approach. Other rewards may include a discretionary Corporate Bonus and/ or Incentives, if eligible. In addition, we offer a comprehensive and high value benefit package to meet the unique needs of our employees and their families, and we are committed to fostering a flexible work environment that enables employees to thrive personally and professionally. Examples of our benefits include retirement plan, health and wellbeing, dental, vision, and pharmacy coverage, health savings account, flexible spending accounts and commuter program, employee assistance program, life and disability insurance, adoption assistance, back-up childcare, tuition/CFA reimbursement and paid time off (leave of absence, paid holidays, volunteer, sick and vacation time). We believe that this approach ultimately supports our mission to deliver investment excellence to our clients and their beneficiaries over the long term.

jobs.title: Audit IT Assurance Intern - Phoenix at Grant Thornton
jobs.description: Employer: Grant Thornton Expires: 10/06/2026 Please apply to the one position/location you are most interested in. In order to be considered for this position, you must apply through the Grant Thornton Job portal at www.grantthornton.com/careers (including resume and transcript). Who is Grant Thornton? At Grant Thornton, we believe in making business more personal and building trust into every result – for our clients and you. Here, we go beyond your expectations of a career in professional services by offering a career path with more: more opportunity, more flexibility, and more support. It’s what makes us different, and we think being different makes us better. In the U.S., Grant Thornton delivers professional services through two specialized entities: Grant Thornton LLP, a licensed, certified public accounting (CPA) firm that provides audit and assurance services ― and Grant Thornton Advisors LLC (not a licensed CPA firm), which exclusively provides non-attest offerings, including tax and advisory services. In 2025, Grant Thornton formed a multinational, multidisciplinary platform with Grant Thornton Ireland. The platform offers a premier Trans-Atlantic advisory and tax practice, as well as independent American and Irish audit practices. With $2.7 billion in revenues and more than 50 offices spanning the U.S., Ireland and other territories, the platform delivers a singular client experience that includes enhanced solutions and capabilities, backed by powerful technologies and a roster of 12,000 quality-driven professionals enjoying exceptional career-growth opportunities and a distinctive cross-border culture. Grant Thornton is part of the Grant Thornton International Limited network, which provides access to its member firms in more than 150 global markets. What is IT Audit Assurance? An IT Assurance Associate is responsible for delivering a full range of IT audit services to our clients. Responsibilities include testing and assessment of information systems control review engagements in support of financial statement audits. Why become an IT Audit Assurance Intern at Grant Thornton? As an IT Audit Assurance Intern at Grant Thornton, your primary responsibility will be to delivering a full range of IT audit services to our clients. This includes testing and assessment of information systems control review engagements in support of financial statement audits. You will work alongside Partners, Managers, and Senior Executives as a member of the engagement team. Additional job responsibilities will include, but will not be limited to, the following: Applying current knowledge of IT trends and systems processes to identify security and risk management issues, as well as other opportunities for overall process improvement. Maintaining professionalism and rapport with the client. Proactively interact with key client management to manage expectations, help ensure client satisfaction, meet client deadlines, and resolve any problems. Gaining a comprehensive understanding of assigned client operations, processes and business objectives, and then utilize that knowledge on assigned engagements. Participating in recruiting efforts as needed. To meet or exceed IT Assurance metrics (e.g. – billable hours, CPE, time delinquencies, etc.). Participating in other business development activities as appropriate. Other duties as assigned. Qualifications Pursuing Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Information Technology, MIS or related field. A Master’s degree is a plus. Minimum overall GPA of 3.0/4.0 Desire to pursue CPA, CISA, CISSP, CIA or CISM license/certification. Some related work experience in public accounting or equivalent delivering controls based services, auditing Information Technology General Controls (ITGC’s.) in support of financial statement audits to cross-industry clients and technologies. An understanding of generally accepted practices for testing Key Reports, and Application Controls a plus. Information Security experience or information security training is required. Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for employment-based visa sponsorship now or in the future. No visa sponsorship is available for this position. Skill Requirements Exceptional client service and communication skills. Strong technical aptitude and problem solving skills Excellent analytical, communication (written and verbal) and interpersonal skills. Effective project and time management skills for handling multiple priorities and simultaneous projects. Enthusiasm to learn through a combination of structured, on-the-job and self-directed training. Ability to work efficiently and effectively in a complex team environment. Strong computer skills including proficiency in Microsoft Office suite applications. Ability to work additional hours and/or travel as needed. The team you’re about to join is ready to help you thrive. Here’s how: Whether it’s your work location, weekly schedule or flex time off, we empower you with the options to work in the way that best serves your clients and your life. jobs.title: Data for Integrity: Regional Analysis and Innovation Internship at Inter-American Development Bank
jobs.description: Employer: Inter-American Development Bank Expires: 10/07/2026 Data for Integrity: Regional Analysis and Innovation InternshipCity: Washington DCCompany: IDBPosting End Date: 9/25/2026 11:59 PM ESTWe improve livesThe IDB Group is a community of diverse, versatile, and passionate people who come together on a journey to improve lives in Latin America and the Caribbean. Our people find purpose and do what they love in an inclusive, collaborative, agile, and rewarding environment.About this positionThe IDB Group is looking for an active graduate student to be hired as an intern under the Consultant modality. The 2027 Winter Internship Program is a competitive paid opportunity, based in Headquarters, for university students from member countries to learn about development work and corporate management of the Bank, and to acquire work experience at the professional level through on-the-job learning.The Institutional Capacity of the State Division (ICS) is seeking a graduate intern to support its Transparency and Integrity thematic area in developing an innovative, web-based analytical tool for Latin America and the Caribbean. The assignment will contribute to the Bank’s efforts to strengthen evidence-based policy dialogue and operational engagement on transparency, integrity, financial integrity, and state effectiveness.Building off the team’s existing diagnostic tools, the intern will develop a working proof of concept for an interactive regional dashboard that brings together internationally recognized indicators and secondary evidence on countries’ transparency and integrity systems. The tool will organize information across three analytical dimensions: enabling conditions, institutional capacity, and risk management. It will allow users to explore country profiles, compare selected countries and indicators, examine trends, and access the underlying sources and methodological information.The dashboard will also support the production of Country Integrity Snapshots, concise analytical briefs that synthesize the available evidence into accessible country-level profiles. The assignment will draw on the team’s existing analytical work, remain distinct from a full diagnostic assessment.The internship offers an opportunity to combine applied data science, interactive visualization, and institutional analysis in a practical development context. The successful candidate will work with Bank specialists to translate an existing analytical concept into a functional prototype that can demonstrate the value of integrated country evidence and provide a foundation for potential future development.What you’ll doCompile, validate, and structure the agreed international indicators and secondary evidence for selected countries, including source metadata, definitions, and methodological limitations.Develop a working web dashboard proof of concept that enables interactive exploration of country profiles, selected indicators, trends, and cross-country comparisons.Integrate source documentation and develop functionality to generate or export standardized Country Integrity Snapshots from the underlying data.Prepare concise, evidence-based interpretations of country patterns and demonstrate how the tool can support regional analysis, policy dialogue, and further country-level assessment.Deliver the functional prototype, supporting data and code, technical documentation, and a final demonstration with recommendations for potential future development.What you'll needEducation: An active graduate student (master’s or Ph.D.) student in Data Science, Computer Science, Computational Social Science, Statistics, Economics, Public Policy, International Development, Information Systems, or a closely related field from an accredited University. The graduation date should be after the Internship period.Languages: Fluency in English with a working knowledge of one other Bank language (Spanish, French, or Portuguese) is a plus.Key Skills: Learn continuously, collaborate and share knowledge, focus on clients, communicate and influence, innovate and try new thingsSoft Skills: Result-driven, collaborative, innovative, client-oriented, strong communicator, self-motivated, eager to learn, and excellent time management skills.Technical skills: Strong analytical and communication skills, with familiarity with transparency, integrity, anti-corruption, financial integrity, and international development; ability to integrate data from multiple sources and develop user-friendly analytical products, with experience in interactive dashboards, Python or R, and AI-assisted tools desirable.RequirementsCitizenship: Be a national of an IDB member country.Active student: Enrolled in a graduate (master’s or Ph.D.) program as of the starting date of the internship program. The graduation date should be after the Internship period.Consanguinity: Not have family members (up to the fourth degree of consanguinity and second degree of affinity, including spouse) working at the IDB or IDB Invest.First job at the IDB Group: Be a first-time participant in an Internship Program held by the Bank or Inter-American Investment Corporation (“Corporation” also known as “IDB Invest”). In addition, you have not been a former staff member, Complementary Workforce (“CW”), contractor for the Bank or the Corporation, or have previously provided services to the Bank or the Corporation through a contractor or under any other contractual modality.Notes:Submit your resume, academic transcripts (official or unofficial), and university letter certifying your student status when applying.If you submit an unofficial academic transcript at the time of applying, you will be requested to present an official one if moving forward.Academic transcripts and university letters should be issued within the last three months.For graduate students a minimum of 50% of coursework must be completed when applying.Applications without the requested documentation will be disqualified.Save each file in a PDF format with your name and subject.DO NOT send copies of your degree certificates or other courses.You must be available to work full-time (40 hours per week) from January 16th to March 15th, 2027. These dates are fixed and cannot be modified. Interns must complete their assignments within this period.If you are an international student in the U.S.A., your work authorization is through CPT or OPT. Consult your school advisor before applying. You must be able to work 40 hours per week, many international students are limited to working part-time, depending on their academic standing.Type of contract and durationType of contract: Intern ConsultantLength of contract: Two (2) monthsDates of the contract: January 16th to March 15th, 2027Location: Washington, D.C. – United States of America*Internship dates may be adjusted slightly to accommodate holidays.Our cultureAt the IDB, we work so everyone brings their best and authentic selves to work while finding their purpose. Our people consistently strive for excellence, and we recognize and celebrate the impact of their contributions.In our efforts to drive innovation, we intentionally include all voices, cultivate a sense of belonging and champion fairness. We welcome individuals from underrepresented groups to join us and share their unique perspectives.We ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations to participate in the job interview process. If you require an accommodation to complete this application, please email us at accommodations@iadb.org.About the IDB Group About the IDB Group The IDB Group, composed of the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB), IDB Invest, and the IDB Lab offers flexible financing solutions to its member countries to finance economic and social development through lending and grants to public and private entities in Latin America and the Caribbean. About IDB We work to improve lives in Latin America and the Caribbean. Through financial and technical support for countries working to reduce poverty and inequality, we help improve health and education and advance infrastructure. Our aim is to achieve development in a sustainable, climate-friendly way. With a history dating back to 1959, today we are the leading source of development financing for Latin America and the Caribbean. We provide loans, grants, and technical assistance; and we conduct extensive research. We maintain a strong commitment to achieving measurable results and the highest standards of integrity, transparency, and accountability. About IDB Invest IDB Invest, a member of the IDB Group, is a multilateral development bank committed to promoting the economic development of its member countries in Latin America and the Caribbean through the private sector. IDB Invest finances sustainable companies and projects to achieve financial results and maximize economic, social, and environmental development in the region. With a portfolio of $14.1 billion in asset management and 325 clients in 25 countries, IDB Invest provides innovative financial solutions and advisory services that meet the needs of its clients in a variety of industries. Follow us: https://www.linkedin.com/company/inter-american-development-bank/ https://www.facebook.com/IADB.org https://twitter.com/the_IDB

jobs.description: Employer: Confluence Environmental Center, AmeriCorps Program Expires: 10/07/2026 Dates of Service October 21st, 2026 – July 29th, 2027 (1,200 hours, approx. 32 hours/week) POSITION TITLEDepave for Trees Coordinator Project PARTNEROregon Walks and Depavehttps://oregonwalks.org/https://www.depave.org/ Position SummaryThis position is in partnership between the Confluence Environmental Center, AmeriCorps Program, DePave and Oregon Walks. 82nd Avenue is in the middle of major public reinvestment, and one of the clearest calls from the community has been for less pavement and more green space, especially trees. This position exists to answer that call on the ground: designing a new "micro-depaving" pilot program that partners directly with private landowners to remove small sections of pavement, plant a tree, and support the landowner in maintaining it. This position will build the relationships and evidence base for a micro-depaving program model through community outreach, education, and partnership building to support increased access to greenspaces along 82nd Avenue.Estimated time breakdown: 40% research, pilot program design; 30% outreach, recruitment, and education; up to 10% project fundraising; and 20% Confluence cohort/leadership development activities. The AmeriCorps Volunteer will participate in Confluence-led leadership development activities which include: Leadership Development Training Series, team meetings, National Service events and other self-directed development opportunities (20%). Essential Functions (to include, but not limited to):Research and design a "micro-depaving" program model for small-scale private-lot depaving projects along the 82nd Avenue corridor including explanations on how to identify sites, how to engage with land owners, how to navigate permitting, and how to contract with partners.Outreach to private landowners along 82nd Avenue to identify potential participantsBuild and maintain relationships with community and technical partners, including the 82nd Avenue Coalition, BRANCH Coalition partners, the City of Portland, and local workforce development organizations.Coordinate with City of Portland permitting staff to understand how the program design stays within permit-exempt thresholds.Identify and define project metrics, outcomes, and narratives to support project sustainability including information about the history of over paving, its impacts on the community, and the importance of depaving and tree canopy development.Complete and submit all necessary paperwork and reports in a timely manner; attend and complete all training and service requirements; wear Confluence uniform and/or appropriate identifiers and required safety gear while performing service or attending official events.Abide by program and AmeriCorps policies. Under no circumstances will AmeriCorps Volunteers be asked to perform prohibited activities outlined in the approved grant. Position RequirementsDeep interest in environmental justice, urban forestry, and environmental work.Comfortable engaging directly with private landowners and community members from a wide range of backgrounds; lived experience in community organizing or outreach is valued equally with formal education.Written and verbal communication skills to draft outreach materials, meeting notes, and grant application materials (specific grant-writing experience is not required but is a benefit).Regular and reliable attendance and dependability; ability to serve as part of a team spanning two host organizations.Willingness/openness to learn about and discuss racial equity and social justice issues.Regular and reliable attendance and dependability. AmeriCorps Volunteers must be: 17 years of age or older at beginning of service term; U.S. citizen, national or lawful permanent resident; in possession of a high school diploma or equivalent, or commit to earning one prior to receiving education award; able to commit to the full term of service; able to successfully pass a fingerprint criminal history background check and satisfactory report from the National Sex Offender Public Website (NSOPW) prior to the start of the position.Ability to serve as part of a diverse team. Preferred QualificationsBilingual or multilingual skills relevant to 82nd Avenue's communities (e.g., Spanish, Vietnamese, Chinese).Experience or coursework in urban forestry, landscape design, environmental science, or a related field.Familiarity with East Portland or the 82nd Avenue corridor.Experience with data tracking tools (Excel, Google Sheets) or basic GIS/mapping.Experience organizing or facilitating community events or volunteer work. Member Benefits Include$15,200 living allowance paid over the 8-month term of service (approx. $1,688 monthly, before taxes). $5,176 education award (qualified student loans and/or education expenses) Loan Forbearance Health Care InsuranceChild Care Reimbursement Option$50 Training Fund Professional Leadership Certificate, Trainings and Networking opportunities. May be eligible for Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP).Monthly TriMet passes available.Access to a Member Assistance Program (free counseling, health & financial tips, etc.)Access to a large network of partner organizationsAccess to events, networking, professional development, and conferencesThe knowledge that you’re working on important environmental justice issues facing tens of thousands of folks in east Portland Project Location & Transportation InformationMember’s office space will be at Depave's Portland office located at River Street Studios (820 N River St, Portland OR) in Portland's inner east side. In person organizing/canvassing and site visits will largely occur on/near 82nd Avenue.Portland has a robust public transit network between the office space and 82nd Avenue. jobs.description: Employer: Trillium Trading - Trillium Trading Expires: 10/08/2026 Trillium is a leading proprietary trading firm active in US Equities, US Options, Canadian Equities, and OTC Equities. With trading technology built, tested, and optimized in-house, our engineers and technologists collaborate with our traders to deliver tools and functionality designed to support their needs. Working closely with a designated trader mentor, you will research and enhance existing trading strategies, develop an understanding of the U.S., Canadian, and OTC equity markets and U.S. options, and strengthen the communication, quantitative, analytical, and decision-making skills required to succeed in a trading environment.Throughout the program, you will practice making simulated, split-second buy and sell decisions using Trillium’s proprietary keyboard-based trading platform. You will also participate in trade review, market research, educational sessions, and direct interactions with experienced traders and trading leadership.Our internship is designed to be a direct pipeline into Trillium’s full-time Equity Trader program. We use the six-week program to give students meaningful exposure to the work, culture, and expectations of a Trillium trader while also giving our team the opportunity to evaluate interns over an extended period. jobs.description: Employer: Made Smarter Yorkshire & Humber Expires: 10/08/2026 Enhanced Control Solutions (ECS) is a growing UK-based SME specialising in engineering and technology, with a focus on keeping modern manufacturing running efficiently and effectively. Built by engineers, we combine hands-on automation expertise with innovative digital solutions to support some of the UK’s leading manufacturers across the food & beverage, pharmaceutical, automotive, packaging, utilities and wider industrial sectors.Our services span automation projects, 24/7 remote engineering support, OT asset and data management, and flexible engineering resource. We are committed to continued growth, innovation and digital transformation, developing practical solutions that help our customers improve reliability, efficiency and resilience.Internship OverviewWe are offering a 12-week Digital Internship to support the continued development of our cybersecurity and digital capabilities. You will contribute to a focused project reviewing our current IT, cloud and digital environments, helping to identify cybersecurity risks and opportunities for improvement. A key focus will be supporting the ongoing development of Connect, our patent-pending remote OT connection technology, helping us ensure that as the technology evolves, it continues to meet recognised cybersecurity best practice and provides a secure and resilient solution for our customers.Location: Wetherby – primarily office-based during initial training, with the opportunity for hybrid working thereafter.Commitment: 37.5 hours per weekThis internship will provide practical experience in applying cybersecurity principles and digital technologies within a real-world engineering and manufacturing environment.What You’ll Gain• Hands-on experience working across cybersecurity, IT, cloud technology and Operational Technology (OT) within a growing engineering and technology SME.• Practical experience in cybersecurity risk assessment, asset and data mapping, access control, vulnerability management, cloud security, backups, incident response and secure remote connectivity.• Exposure to recognised cybersecurity frameworks and standards, including ISO/IEC 27001, IEC 62443 and Cyber Essentials.• The opportunity to contribute to the cybersecurity development of Connect, our innovative, patent-pending remote OT technology.• Experience of applying cybersecurity principles within a commercial environment and understanding the balance between security, engineering requirements and customer needs.• Mentorship and guidance from experienced engineering and technology professionals.• Insight into potential career pathways across cybersecurity, IT and OT security.Project ResponsibilitiesWorking with support from the ECS team, the role will contribute to a defined 12-week cybersecurity improvement project. Responsibilities are expected to include:• Supporting the mapping of ECS's Connect and Command Centre systems, including infrastructure, cloud services, software components, users, access routes, data flows, logging, backups and relevant third-party services.• Helping to create and validate inventories of key IT and OT-related assets, software, data and suppliers.• Reviewing existing cybersecurity controls and identifying potential risks, vulnerabilities and areas for improvement.• Supporting a baseline gap assessment against appropriate cybersecurity good practice and relevant frameworks such as ISO/IEC 27001, IEC 62443 and Cyber Essentials.• Reviewing areas such as user access, MFA, privileged accounts, device security, patching, backups, encryption, remote access, logging and incident response.• Researching appropriate technical solutions and good practice where potential improvements are identified.• Helping to document existing controls, processes and technical arrangements in a clear and structured way.• Supporting the cybersecurity review of ECS's patent-pending remote OT connection technology, helping to assess its architecture, access controls, data flows, remote connectivity and security controls against recognised cybersecurity good practice.• Working with ECS engineers, developers and management to understand how cybersecurity requirements need to work alongside practical engineering and customer requirements.• Producing a final summary of findings and contributing to a prioritised cybersecurity improvement roadmap, identifying recommended actions, priorities and potential next steps for ECS.By the end of the 12-week internship, the successful candidate will have contributed to a documented cybersecurity baseline and prioritised improvement roadmap for ECS, including recommendations to support the continued secure development of our Connect remote OT technology and Command Centre platform.Who Should ApplyWe are looking for someone who:• Is studying towards or has recently completed a degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Computing, Software Engineering, Networking, Digital Technology, Engineering or another relevant discipline.• Has an interest in developing a career in cybersecurity, IT, software, cloud technology or Operational Technology (OT) security.• Has good communication skills and the confidence to ask questions and work with people from different technical backgrounds.• Is curious, practical and keen to learn, with an ability to look beyond theory and consider how cybersecurity controls can be implemented effectively within a real business environment.Candidates must be able to start immediatelyCandidates must accept or decline an internship within 5 working days of an offer being madePlease make us aware if you have a disability, long-term health condition or any access requirements, please let us know if there are any reasonable adjustments we can make to support you throughout the application and selection process. Any information you provide will be treated confidentially, used only to help us arrange the appropriate support, and will not affect your application in any way.Candidates must accept or decline an internship within 5 working days of an offer being madeEquality, Diversity and Inclusion StatementWe are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and experiences and value the different perspectives they can bring to our team. Selection will be based on skills, potential and enthusiasm for developing a career in digital technology and cybersecurity.If you have any specific questions relating to the role, please contact Emma Chapman at service@ecs-uk.com.

jobs.title: Underwriting Summer Intern at Odyssey Group
jobs.description: Employer: Odyssey Group Expires: 10/09/2026 2027 Summer Intern, UnderwritingThe CompanyOdysseyRe is the reinsurance arm of the Odyssey Group, a global insurance and reinsurance enterprise wholly owned by Fairfax Financial Holdings Limited. OdysseyRe offers a broad range of property, casualty, and specialty reinsurance solutions through a network of branch and representative offices around the world. OdysseyRe’s Underwriting Division evaluates insurance risks on both a portfolio basis (Treaty reinsurance) and an individual risk basis (Facultative reinsurance). The principal responsibilities of an underwriter are to conduct an in-depth review of a Treaty or Facultative business opportunity by reviewing data and other relevant documents, determining the level of risk, and ultimately deciding if OdysseyRe should support the deal. Underwriters are client-facing and represent OdysseyRe in the market, working closely with reinsurance brokers and insurance company clients to negotiate transactions. In coordination with other departments to evaluate reinsurance opportunities, underwriters are the key revenue generators and the decisions they make are key to the Company’s performance. The OpportunityOdysseyRe’s Underwriting Internship Program is a 10-week rotational program offering a unique perspective of the reinsurance industry. As an intern, you will rotate through several underwriting divisions (Property Treaty, Casualty Treaty, Casualty Facultative, Accident and Health, etc.) to learn reinsurance basics, the day-to-day responsibilities of an underwriter, and the intricacies of each market. These foundational experiences will develop your technical skills and provide you with an understanding of our underwriting philosophy, which will endow you with the necessary skills to help underwrite new and renewal business. Several projects will be assigned during your rotations and the program will culminate with a presentation to senior management outlining your overall experience. If you are eager to learn and possess strong interpersonal skills, this is the role for you. You will engage with senior leaders daily and build your network at a variety industry events over the course of the summer. QualificationsThe Underwriting Internship Program is open to highly motivated students who are in their junior year of an undergraduate program and meet the following criteria: GPA 3.2 and aboveExceptional presentation and communication skills, both verbal and written Excellent interpersonal skillsAnalytical thinker with strong attention to detailDemonstrated leadership abilities through college or community activitiesTeam-oriented with the ability to work independently This is a hybrid role requiring 4 days in-office and 1 day remote each week, based out of our Stamford, CT office with occasional travel to New York City (approximately 20% of the time). #LI-Hybrid

jobs.description: Employer: Saja Expires: 10/09/2026 About SAJASAJA is building a new way to collect, trade, and engage with physical collectibles through a digital-first experience. jobs.description: Employer: California Bank and Trust Expires: 10/09/2026 California Bank & Trust’s Internship and Banker Development Program positions are not eligible for employment visa sponsorship (e.g., H-1B visa). This includes, for example, situations where a candidate may have temporary work authorization while enrolled in school or upon graduation (e.g., CPT, OPT) but would need H-1B visa sponsorship within a few years of employment in order to maintain employment eligibility. Associates at California Bank & Trust work in a relationship-centered culture where they are provided with the tools, training, and opportunities to build the best possible relationships with our clients and with each other. Our workplace culture values each associate’s unique experiences, background and perspectives and provides a collaborative environment for all employees to grow and thrive. As a premier California-focused financial services company dedicated to serving its communities, families, and businesses (small, mid-sized and large), CB&T has been active for 70 years and has more than 80 full-service branch offices across the state. This dedication has helped the bank earn recognition as a perennial powerhouse in yearly voting for “Best Bank” and “Best Commercial Bank” from the readers of San Diego Union-Tribune and Orange County Register. Additionally, as a division of Zions Bancorporation, the bank has collected multiple Greenwich Excellence Awards for “Overall Client Satisfaction” in Small Business & Middle Market Excellence Awards. We are currently looking for our next class of Rotational Banking Interns. This 8-week full-time is available for current college students. California Bank & Trust’s Summer Internship Program gives students the opportunity to gain valuable and practical work experience in their majors, explore the banking/finance industry, and learn about our culture and business philosophy. Each intern will rotate through various departments, allowing students to gain experience in several areas of banking and explore different career alternatives and choices. Duties include but are not limited to: conducting industry research, preparing client prospect lists, assisting with credit presentations, and observing the process of spreading financial statements and underwriting loans. The internship experience also includes several networking events with executives and other managers around the Bank, professional development and training sessions, case studies, overviews of various areas of the Bank, and social events. The combination of hands-on assignments, programmed trainings, and events provides each intern with a well-rounded summer experience. Former interns have gained exposure to areas such as:Commercial BankingFinanceReal Estate Minimum Qualifications:Must be currently enrolled in a College/University and be within 1 year of graduation at the time of internship. jobs.description: Employer: California Bank and Trust Expires: 10/09/2026 California Bank & Trust’s Internship and Banker Development Program positions are not eligible for employment visa sponsorship (e.g., H-1B visa). Our workplace culture values each associate’s unique experiences, background and perspectives and provides a collaborative environment for all employees to grow and thrive. jobs.title: Payments Forum Intern - Spring/Summer 2027 at Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta
jobs.description: Employer: Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta Expires: 10/09/2026 As an employee of the Atlanta Fed, you will help support our mission of promoting the stability and efficiency of the U.S. economy and financial system. Your work will affect the economy of the Southeast, the United States, and the world. The work we do here is important, and how we do it is just as important as what we do. We live our values of integrity, excellence, and respect every day. We do the right thing, we do things right, and we treat people right. A career at the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta gives you the chance to do work that touches lives and helps communities prosper. The Bank believes in flexibility to balance the demands of work and life while also recognizing the necessity of connecting and collaborating with our colleagues in person. Onsite work is an essential function of this position, and you are required to be onsite according to the schedule set by your management. The Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta Research Department is now hiring for our Spring and Summer 2027 Internship Program. This is an onsite/ hybrid (Preferred) or remote position eligible; candidate must be available to work 15 hours a week during the Spring semester (January – early May): Monday-Friday 8AM-5PM EST; and 30 hours a week during the Summer semester (late May – early August) during the following days/times: Monday – Friday 8AM – 5PM EST. Opportunity exists to work on-site during the Summer semester to engage in the Atlanta Fed’s broader internship program offerings. The position will start January 2027 through August 2027*. The Research Division focuses on every aspect of the economy, from the local to the international level. At the Atlanta Fed, studies range from analyzing rural banking markets in the Southeast to designing and testing economic forecasting models used in policy making. *date subject to change SCOPE OF ASSIGNMENT Payments Forum – Selected students will be conducting recruitment of depository and financial institutions, major card networks, payments processors, and card issuers through data submission and validation activities as part of the Federal Reserve Payments Study (FRPS) administered by the Atlanta Fed’s Payments Forum in partnership with the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. The FRPS is the most comprehensive, unbiased study of noncash payments activity in the U.S. The FRPS collects data from some 4,000 financial institutions and more than 100 network processors and issuers. Encouraging these respondents to participate and helping them to do so is the goal of the Research Interns. More information about the FRPS can be found here. QUALIFICATIONSPreference will be given to candidates willing to make a two-semester commitment (Spring/Summer 2027).Currently enrolled as an undergraduate or graduate student, preferably in economics.Excellent verbal and written communication skills.Creative thinking and problem-solving skills.Organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to meet deadlines. OUR BENEFITS TO INTERNS (some benefits are subject to being onsite): Professional development opportunities Networking MARTA passes provided Free LinkedIn Learning access Free access to our FedFuel career development tool Café and dining options on-site Dress for your day Flexible hours Access to on-site fitness center Additional Requirements: This position will require at minimum fingerprinting for a criminal background check, education and employment verification, along with potential additional screening requirements due to the information accessed while performing the job. Any offer of employment is contingent upon satisfactory results of any required background screening. These screenings would be initiated at the time of offer acceptance and can take up to approximately 8 weeks to be completed. The screening covers areas such as education/employment verification, criminal history, credit history, and reaches out to your references and people that know you well. For Law Enforcement positions, physical, psychological, drug, stress/EKG, and attending an academy will be required. Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States without the need for visa sponsorship now or in the future. Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta employees must comply with the Bank’s ethics rules. These rules generally prohibit employees, their spouses/domestic partners, and minor children from holding financial interests (such as common stock and corporate bonds) issued by financial institutions. This prohibition also applies to investment funds that focus on investing in the financial sector. If you, your spouse/domestic partner, or minor child own such securities, you will generally be asked to divest them if you accept an offer of Bank employment. If you have concerns about this prohibition, you should raise the issue with the recruiter for this posting early in the process. jobs.title: Logistics Summer Intern at Bath & Body Works
jobs.description: Employer: Bath & Body Works Expires: 10/09/2026 Description At Bath & Body Works, we believe everybody deserves to feel good. When you join us, you're part of more than an iconic fragrance and personal care brand — you become part of Gingham Nation, where people are at the center of everything we do. We believe great associate experiences create great consumer experiences. When our associates feel supported, inspired and empowered, consumers feel it. Whether you're starting your career or building your next chapter, we invest in your growth so you can learn, lead and help create feel good moments every day. Internship Overview Our internship program gives a dynamic group of emerging, high potential rising university seniors the opportunity to participate in a 10-week summer internship at an iconic brand and industry leader in personal care and home fragrance. This internship will provide the opportunity for a comprehensive view of the various functional areas within the brand. You will have the opportunity to work alongside and learn from B&BW associates who will provide training, development and engagement of your function and our brand. Our internship program is a key driver of our early career talent pool through realistic job previews and meaningful projects and assignments. Your ideas and insights will be meaningful and valued in influencing our business. We are looking for interns to learn and support our business strategies through curiosity, a passion for retail and a can-do attitude. B&BW interns will have the following development opportunities: Mentorship and career development Professional development workshops Functional and brand learning Networking, social and philanthropy opportunities with fellow interns and business associates to develop relationships with each other and key leaders within B&BW Total Rewards Package for Summer Interns Competitive hourly wages Furnished housing or living stipend (eligibility requirements) Personal days & Summer Fridays 40% Merchandise Discount Hybrid working (function dependent) Successful interns could be considered for a full-time job upon completion. Program Areas Logistics & OperationsOur full-service logistics operation is focused on delivering flexible and scalable global supply chain solutions – built on a foundation of expertise in the fundamentals: transportation, warehousing, distribution, and fulfillment. At Bath & Body Works, the logistics team is coordinating the movement of our products from sourcing origins and factories throughout the world to our distribution centers in the U.S to our retail’s stores and direct costumers. Our logistics is a strategic business that drives real value throughout best-in-class supply chain engineering’s, customer and trade compliance, warehousing, and management of global and regional distribution centers. Logistics Intern Responsibilities:Provide leadership to non-exempt, distribution center associates. Demonstrate effective communication skills with associates, peers and leadership in a variety of business functions. Make effective product flow decisions under the direction of the Manager.Positively impact levels of service and cost on the Distribution Center's operation plans. Support projects to procure capacity for specific segments of the supply chain such as the Bath & Body Works Regional Fulfillment center inbound program or review of our lanes for dedicated program capacity Qualifications University current juniors pursuing their bachelor’s degree and in good academic standing Must be able to work 40 hours per week during summer 2027 June 1st August 6th (required dates) No extended PTO Computer fluency with programs such as Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, Excel Innate curiosity and desire to learn, strong analytical and logical thinking skills Strong organizational skills and ability to multi-task and prioritize Have a strong passion for retail Preferred Qualifications Previous internship, customer service or leadership experience Ability to manage through conflict and problem-solve Strong communication and presentation skills; can concisely present complex information/recommendations in terms meaningful to various audiences Able to work in a fast-paced environment Core Competencies Drives Results Action Oriented Collaborates Decision Making Nimble Learning About Us Bath & Body Works is a global leader in personal care and home fragrance, driven by the belief that everybody deserves to feel good. The brand’s beloved and iconic scents are expertly crafted for exceptional performance and a luxury fragrance experience. Formulated with thoughtfully chosen ingredients, Bath & Body Works’ body care products are available in multiple forms including fine fragrance mist, body cream, lotion, eau de parfum, body wash, hand soap, sanitizer and more. The brand’s famous 3-wick candles are made with rich, high-quality fragrance oils layered throughout a premium soy wax base, for up to 45 hours of room-filling fragrance. Consumers can shop Bath & Body Works anytime and anywhere they choose, from welcoming, in-store experiences at more than 1,900 stores in the U.S. and Canada, 550-plus international locations and select Ulta Beauty stores. Online, consumers can visit bathandbodyworks.com, Amazon and Ulta.com.

jobs.description: Employer: Kroll Expires: 10/09/2026 Portfolio Valuation - Intern Join Kroll’s Global Portfolio Valuation team for a hands-on summer internship analyzing complex, illiquid investments across a wide range of industries and asset types. You will receive structured training, work alongside experienced valuation professionals and contribute to real client engagements while building practical financial modeling, research and communication skills.As a market leader in illiquid portfolio pricing and valuation, Kroll assists clients in valuing alternative investments, including securities and positions for which active-market quotations are not available. Our teams assess investments ranging from debt and equity securities to convertible instruments, warrants and options. Analysts gain experience supporting engagements involving individual investments and entire portfolios while learning how to develop independent, transparent and supportable valuation conclusions. Throughout the internship, you will receive training and guidance from experienced professionals, collaborate with team members and gain insight into career opportunities within Portfolio Valuation. You will have the opportunity to apply what you have learned in the classroom to meaningful assignments while developing a stronger understanding of alternative investments and the valuation profession.At Kroll, your work will help deliver clarity to our clients’ most complex governance, risk, and transparency challenges. Apply now to join One team, One Kroll.RESPONSIBILITIES:Are you intellectually curious, comfortable working through complex financial questions and motivated to learn alongside others? As a Portfolio Valuation Intern, you will combine financial analysis, research, communication and teamwork to help our professionals value investments that do not have readily observable market prices.Portfolio Valuation Interns support valuation advisory services for the alternative investment community, including private equity and hedge funds, business development companies, pensions and endowments. During the internship, you will contribute to engagements involving illiquid and complex investment positions while learning how teams develop analyses that are independent, well-supported and clearly communicated.Assist in building and updating financial models using discounted cash flow, market multiple, market transaction and option-pricing analyses Support valuation analyses for illiquid debt, equity and other alternative investments across a range of industries and geographies using accepted valuation approaches and relevant financial theory Research companies, industries, capital markets and comparable transactions to help identify information and assumptions relevant to each analysis Gain exposure to investments that may include debt securities, preferred and common equity, convertible securities, warrants, options, structured products, whole-loan pools and real estate Review financial statements, investment documents, portfolio-company information and market data under the guidance of experienced team members Participate in client discussions and meetings to observe how teams gather financial, operational and investment-specific information relevant to an engagement Collaborate with team members to evaluate assumptions, address analytical questions and complete accurate, high-quality work within engagement timelines Assist in preparing workpapers, valuation schedules, written reports and presentation materials that clearly explain the analysis and resulting conclusions Gain exposure to projects involving individual investments, entire portfolios and reviews of clients’ valuation policies and practices Contribute to a strong client experience by communicating professionally, responding thoughtfully to feedback and working effectively with colleagues at all levels Participate in training, networking opportunities and relevant industry events to strengthen your technical knowledge and understanding of the alternative asset industry REQUIREMENTS:Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, Management, Engineering or a related analytical discipline from an accredited college or university; candidates in Engineering should have completed junior- or senior-level coursework in Accounting, Economics or Finance Graduation date between December 2027 and September 2028 Cumulative GPA of 3.2 or higher Foundational knowledge of corporate finance, accounting, economics, financial statement analysis or valuation developed through coursework, student organizations, academic projects or previous work experience Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Word, including the ability to organize data, perform calculations and present information clearly Strong analytical, critical-thinking and problem-solving skills, with an interest in understanding complex investments and financial questionsCareful attention to detail and a commitment to producing accurate, well-supported work Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to ask thoughtful questions, explain your work and incorporate feedback Ability to manage multiple assignments, organize priorities and meet deadlines in a collaborative, fast-paced environment A team-focused and inclusive working style, with the ability to work effectively with colleagues from different backgrounds and areas of expertise Intellectual curiosity, adaptability and a willingness to learn new valuation concepts, industries and investment structures Preferred: Previous internship, academic project, coursework or student-organization experience involving financial analysis, accounting, investments, economics, data analysis or business research Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States without the need for visa sponsorship now or in the future About Kroll Join the global leader in risk and financial advisory solutions—Kroll. With a nearly century-long legacy, we blend trusted expertise with cutting-edge technology to navigate and redefine industry complexities. As a part of One Team, One Kroll, you'll contribute to a collaborative and empowering environment, propelling your career to new heights. Ready to build, protect, restore and maximize our clients’ value? Your journey begins with Kroll. Kroll is committed to creating an inclusive work environment. jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Learning & Development Intern at Optimal Care Services LLC
jobs.description: Employer: Optimal Care Services LLC Expires: 10/09/2026 Learning & Development InternshipNew York City Metropolitan AreaPosition SummaryOptimal Care Services (OCS), New York City’s largest provider of Special Education Itinerant Teacher (SEIT) services, is seeking a motivated intern to manage and enhance our Microsoft Viva Learning platform.This is a hands-on role with real ownership. As the Learning & Development Intern, you will maintain OCS’s central training library, organize onboarding and professional development content, track training completion, and help ensure employees can easily access the resources they need.A key project for this internship is supporting the launch of OCS’s new Early Intervention (EI) Division. You will help build the EI learning library, develop onboarding pathways for new staff, and track required training and credentialing requirements. This is a unique opportunity to help create a training program from the ground up while gaining experience in learning management, content organization, and workforce development. Essential Duties and Responsibilities1. Content Curation and Library ManagementOwn the Viva Learning library: build and maintain a clear taxonomy of categories, tags, and collections so a SEIT teacher, a billing specialist, and a new hire each find what they need in under a minute.Source new learning material on an ongoing basis. from Microsoft Learn, LinkedIn Learning, third-party providers, and OCS's own subject-matter experts, and propose additions monthly rather than waiting to be asked.Vet every item before it is published: check accuracy, relevance to preschool special education practice, currency, accessibility, and licensing. Retire content that is outdated, duplicated, or unused.Publish internally developed content — recorded trainings, SOPs, policy walkthroughs, and onboarding materials — into the library with consistent titles, descriptions, thumbnails, and metadata.Maintain a content calendar so the library refreshes on a predictable cadence and seasonal needs (school-year onboarding, annual policy updates, audit season) are met ahead of time.Build the Early Intervention collection from scratch — source, vet, and publish content covering EI program fundamentals, the IFSP process, family-centered and natural-environment practice, and EI documentation standards, working with the EI Division leads to fill gaps as the division grows.2. Learning Paths and AssignmentsBuild role-based learning paths for the roles OCS staffs: SEIT teacher, related-service provider, Early Intervention provider and service coordinator, supervisor, billing and compliance staff, administrative support, sequencing content so each path is a coherent program rather than a list of links.Assign required training to the appropriate departments and cohorts, set realistic due dates, and coordinate with department managers before assignments go out.Track completions and follow up on outstanding assignments through reminders and escalation to managers, keeping the tone supportive and the records clean.Coordinate onboarding paths with the Human Resources Manager so every new hire receives a complete, current first-week learning assignment on their start date.Design the EI Division onboarding path as the division launches; a first-day-ready sequence for new EI hires that no one has built yet and revise it as the program takes shape.3. Compliance Training TrackingMaintain the master schedule for mandated and regulatory training - NYSED, NYC DOE, and NYS DOH requirements, mandated reporter and child abuse identification, workplace harassment prevention, HIPAA and confidentiality, health and safety, and OCS internal policy attestations.Track Early Intervention requirements as a distinct track: training and credentialing tied to New York State Department of Health Bureau of Early Intervention and NYC Early Intervention Program participation, provider approval and renewal dates, and any EI-specific documentation training. Keep this record audit ready from day one rather than reconstructing it later.Track completion status by employee, department, and requirement, and produce audit-ready documentation that stands up to review by NYSED, the NYC DOE, the NYS DOH, or our external auditors.Work with the Compliance Manager on training-related audit requests and on evidence retention: what was assigned, to whom, when it was completed, and where the record is stored.Surface gaps early: flag approaching deadlines, lapsing certifications, and staff who are at risk of falling out of compliance before a deadline is missed.4. Usage Reporting and AdoptionTurn Viva Learning analytics into a monthly dashboard covering active users, completion rates, most- and least-used content, and adoption by department.Report findings to HR leadership with recommendations: what to promote, what to retire, where a path is too long, and where a department needs a nudge.Promote the platform internally through Teams announcements, short how-to guides, and periodic "what's new in the library" communications that staff will open.Gather staff feedback through short surveys and direct outreach and close the loop by acting on what you hear. Qualifications and RequirementsRequiredCurrently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program — education, instructional design, human resources, information systems, library and information science, communications, or a related field.Available for 20–25 hours per week on a consistent weekly schedule during OCS business hours, including at least three days on site.Strong organizational instincts and genuine attention to detail — this role is judged on whether records are accurate and content is where it should be.Comfort with Microsoft 365, particularly Teams, SharePoint, and Excel; ability to learn Viva Learning administration with training and documentation.Clear written communication — you will write content descriptions, staff announcements, and reminder messages that hundreds of employees read.Discretion with confidential employee and training records.PreferredCoursework or experience in instructional design, curriculum development, adult learning, or knowledge management.Familiarity with learning management systems, SCORM content, or digital content curation in any setting.Interest in special education, early childhood, early intervention, or health and human services.Basic comfort with data such as pivot tables and simple dashboards. Success MeasuresAt the end of the first semester, a successful Site Manager will have:a library with a documented taxonomy, no broken or outdated links, and a written content standard others can followpublished learning paths for at least three OCS roles, with onboarding fully covereda working Early Intervention section — content, onboarding path, and compliance tracker — ready for the division's first cohort of staffa compliance tracker that gives leadership an accurate completion picture on demand, without a scramblea monthly usage report with recommendations, and measurable growth in staff engagement with the platform; brought in new material, on their own initiative, that staff use and ask for more of.Compensation and Terms$20.00 per hour, the OCS standard student rate.Paid sick leave in accordance with New York State and New York City law.Academic credit supported where the student's institution permits; OCS will complete required school documentation and supervisor evaluations.Mentorship from the Human Resources Manager and exposure to compliance, finance, and operations leadership.Schedule flexibility around examinations and academic deadlines, arranged in advance. To ApplySubmit a resume and a note describing a time you organized information for other people to use, and one piece of learning content you would add to a library like ours. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.Optimal Care Services is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We value diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We welcome applicants regardless of economic, linguistic, and cultural differences or physical, learning, and emotional challenges.
